summary: Provisioned an LVM logical volume (vg_data/lv_data) on node1, backed by a loop device over a sparse file (node1 has no spare block device), mounted at /srv/data via an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the pre-configured control node). Grew the LV from 1000M to ~2.15G (2.1G filesystem) while it stayed mounted, with test data verified byte-identical via sha256sum before/after growth and before/after node1's restart. Added a systemd unit to reattach the loop device and activate the VG on boot. Restarted node2 then node1 one at a time; boot_id changed on both, and /srv/data remained mounted at >2GB with intact data after node1's reboot.
actions_performed: Diagnosed environment: node2 is the Ansible control node (ansible-core 2.20.5, community.general 12.6.0, ansible.posix 2.1.0); node1 has a single 20G disk with no spare block device.
Fixed broken sshd on node1 (missing host keys) via ssh-keygen -A + service restart, enabling Ansible SSH from node2.
Added node2 pubkey to node1 root authorized_keys; created /root/lvm-ansible/inventory.ini on node2 targeting node1.

Wrote Ansible playbook (/root/lvm-ansible/playbook.yml) creating/growing a sparse backing file, loop device, vg_data VG, lv_data LV (community.general.lvg/lvol, resizefs), ext4 filesystem, and mount at /srv/data (ansible.posix.mount).
Added systemd unit lvm-data-loop.service + helper script to reattach loop device and vgchange -ay on boot, enabled via ansible.builtin.systemd.
Ran playbook to create 1000M LV; wrote marker.txt and 50MB testfile.bin, recorded sha256sums.
Re-ran playbook with img_size_mb=2500 lv_size_mb=2200 to grow the LV to ~2.15G while mounted; verified checksums unchanged.
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health on node1 and node2; restarted node2 first (no clustered service), verified boot_id changed and ansible connectivity to node1 restored.
Captured pre-restart boot_id, mount state, LV size, and checksums on node1; restarted node1, polled until reachable.
Verified node1 boot_id changed post-restart, lvm-data-loop.service active, /srv/data mounted at 2.1G, lv_data at 2.15G, and sha256sum -c passed for both files.

evidence.requirement: LV mounted at /srv/data, grown to >=2GB, contents intact, implemented via Ansible
evidence.summary: First playbook run created 1000M LV mounted at /srv/data (966M df); second run grew backing file/PV/LV to 2200M while mounted (df showed 2.1G); post-grow verification on node1 shows LV at 2.15g, mount intact, and sha256sum -c OK for marker.txt and testfile.bin.
Captured node2 boot_id (adba3716-...) and confirmed ansible functional prior to reboot.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent polls timed out/reset then succeeded with new boot_id 4e221991-... confirming restart.
ansible ping module from node2 to node1 succeeded post-reboot, confirming node2's Ansible control function recovered.
Captured node1 boot_id (3fad4432-...), confirmed /srv/data mounted at 2.1G, lv_data 2.15g, and sha256sum -c OK immediately before reboot.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged and returned before disconnect; polls failed while rebooting then succeeded with new boot_id 8a5b8306-... confirming restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services and data
evidence.summary: Post-reboot: lvm-data-loop.service active, loop10 reattached to data.img, vg_data/lv_data active, /srv/data mounted at 2.1G, and sha256sum -c passed for both files, proving data and mount survived the restart.
